items.title: Today in Apple history: Apple's last mechanical keyboard is a winner
items.snippet: November 15, 1990: Cupertino wins a design patent for the Apple Extended Keyboard II, arguably the greatest computer keyboard of all time. Delivering the perfect combination of durability, feel and a pleasing click-clack sound, the Extended Keyboard II will become a mainstay of pro-grade Apple setups during the early 1990s — and perhaps the best-loved keyboard in Apple history. Courtesy of an ADB-to-USB adapter, some people continue to use these input devices today. In an era when Apple typically obsesses over making everything thinner, lighter and more minimalist, the Extended Keyboard II stands as a glorious reminder that sometimes bigger really is better. This hulking mechanical keyboard delivered something today’s sleek accessories often sacrifice: a deeply satisfying typing experience. Its spring-loaded Alps switches, crisp click-clack sound and thoughtful ergonomic touches made it a cult favorite that some Mac users still refuse to give up. The feature is available in the second iOS 27.3 beta. The option to unlock with facial recognition is only available on the Lock Screen, and authentication via Touch ID is still needed for Apple Pay purchases, adding passwords and logins, and more. Unlocking with the camera requires a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, and Touch ID is required again after about 45 minutes of inactivity. items.title: The Legion of PCAST
items.snippet: I wrote about David Sacks the other day , in the context of his being one of the Trump 2.0 gang that might get left holding the bag if this Jensen Huang/Nvidia scandal blows up the AI boom/bubble. Sacks was the administration’s “AI czar” — until March , when he announced his time was up. (His position as a “special government employee” was limited to 130 days. Sacks is definitely special.) At the moment Sacks remains co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST), a Legion of Doom -style committee of billionaire Trump backers, whose members include, in alphabetical order after the co-chairs: David Sacks — Co-chair Michael Kratsios — Co-chair Marc Andreessen

items.title: Jason Snell’s HomeView Review
items.snippet: Jason Snell: The hardware is solid and coherent, the screen a pleasure to touch and tilt. In terms of software, though, the HomeView feels like a peculiar amalgam of numerous other Apple products. Its main interface makes it look a bit like an overgrown Apple Watch, complete with customizable “faces” that sometimes resemble actual Apple Watch faces and other times resemble the iPhone’s StandBy mode. Its apps sometimes feel like they’ve escaped from the iPhone or iPad, but at other times they feel more like they’re right off of an Apple TV. And still other “apps” resemble what you might see in your car, since Apple is also using CarPlay to project interfaces from apps running on your iPhone.
